capabilities.label: Document understanding
capabilities.task: Interpreting written or tabular content inside an image or PDF: reading/transcribing text, copying visible fields, or parsing a page/table. Required whenever ANY part of the requested answer needs that content, including alongside categorization. Absent when the work ONLY recognizes whole objects or their categories from appearance without reading content. An object carrying text does not by itself require reading it. Already-extracted plain text is not this capability.
capabilities.benchmark: Reading or interpreting written text, symbols, tables, charts, formulas or layout supplied as visual input, including text embedded in natural scenes. Merely recognizing an object or processing already extracted text is insufficient. The reading operation must contribute to the evaluated answer.

capabilities.label: Structured output
capabilities.task: Extracting or normalizing explicit fields, assigning category labels, or returning data records in a fixed machine-readable structure. Evaluate the requested answer, not the format of the input or what generated code would produce. Organizing prose with headings, paragraphs or bullets does not itself need this capability. Extraction and classification can need it even without a strict output format.
capabilities.benchmark: The benchmark is designed to evaluate compliance with instructions, constraints or output schemas as a primary target. A requested answer marker, multiple-choice letter, JSON wrapper, tool-call syntax or grading/extraction rule is incidental and does NOT establish this capability, even if a malformed answer would fail the task.

capabilities.label: Code & engineering
capabilities.task: The selected model itself must write, edit, review, or debug source code, including generating SQL queries or SQLite SELECT statements. Read-only SQL generation IS code writing. Building a product that uses the model does not by itself make the model a coding model. Calling APIs is not writing code.
capabilities.benchmark: Writing, repairing, reviewing or executing source code or software-engineering tasks.

capabilities.label: Reasoning
capabilities.task: Substantial logical inference, planning, or comparing alternatives. Do not add this for routine extraction or because every task requires some thinking.
capabilities.benchmark: Directly measuring logical, causal, spatial, strategic or conceptual reasoning. Do not add this to every test merely because some reasoning helps.

capabilities.label: Math & science
capabilities.task: Solving mathematical problems, proving theorems, deriving equations, or nontrivial scientific calculations. Mathematical proofs require this capability. Ordinary prose and copying numbers do not.
capabilities.benchmark: Solving mathematical or scientific problems or performing quantitative calculations.

capabilities.label: Knowledge & research
capabilities.task: Factual question answering, research, or subject knowledge beyond copying supplied fields. Recognizing ordinary objects, assigning labels or evaluating supplied rules does not require research or general knowledge.
capabilities.benchmark: Testing factual recall, subject knowledge, factual research or answer correctness beyond supplied content.

capabilities.label: Writing & language
capabilities.task: Producing or revising natural-language prose, translating or summarizing. Required only when the requested output itself contains prose generation or transformation. Comprehending input, selecting a category name, returning a numeric score or extracting data fields is not prose generation. Source code is not prose.
capabilities.benchmark: Measuring prose generation, rewriting, translation, summarization or language completion quality.

capabilities.label: Summarization & synthesis
capabilities.task: Condensing or synthesizing supplied source material into a faithful shorter account: summaries, themes or findings with supporting quotes, digests, meeting notes, or answers grounded only in supplied documents. Required when the deliverable must restate supplied content without adding claims the source does not support. Writing new content from instructions alone, extracting fixed data fields, or answering from general knowledge is not summarization.
capabilities.benchmark: Measuring whether summaries or answers generated from supplied source documents stay faithful to them, such as hallucination or factual-consistency rates against the source, or capture their content. Free composition without a source document, extraction into fixed fields and closed-book factual recall do not establish this.

capabilities.label: Analysis & recommendations
capabilities.task: Applying judgment to supplied or described information to produce a reasoned deliverable: prioritizing items, weighing tradeoffs, assessing causes or impact, or recommending actions with justification, as in business, product or professional work. Formal puzzles, mathematics and source code are not this. Summarizing or reformatting content without judgment is not this.
capabilities.benchmark: Measuring the quality of professional or business analysis deliverables or open-ended expert judgment, such as recommendations, prioritization, plans or reports graded by experts or by human preference on such requests. Formal logic puzzles, mathematics, coding and closed-book trivia do not establish this.

capabilities.label: Visual understanding
capabilities.task: The selected model must interpret supplied visual inputs such as photos, screenshots, scans, or diagrams. Mentioning images that are explicitly excluded does not require vision.
capabilities.benchmark: The evaluated model must interpret supplied images or visual inputs. Producing an image, or reading text that describes one, is insufficient.

capabilities.label: Tools & agents
capabilities.task: Autonomous multi-step execution: plan actions, inspect tool results, and choose further actions in a loop, such as browsing or operating a computer. Inspecting a returned error, correcting arguments and trying a function again is also a required multi-step loop. A single function call, extracting tool arguments, or dispatching to one supplied function does NOT require this capability; the separate tools question covers those. Product names like tool, application, workflow, or agent do not establish a multi-step loop.
capabilities.benchmark: Executing dependent actions in an environment, inspecting results and choosing subsequent actions. Describing agents or a single function dispatch is insufficient.

capabilities.label: Long context
capabilities.task: Reasoning over unusually large supplied inputs, such as hundreds of pages or a large codebase. A long response, a short ongoing conversation, or cross-session persistence alone does not require a large context window.
capabilities.benchmark: Explicitly measuring retrieval or reasoning over unusually long supplied context. Long output or persistent memory alone is insufficient.

capabilities.label: Tool calling
capabilities.task: The model invokes externally provided functions or APIs to complete evaluated work. Selecting functions, forming arguments, executing actions and calling memory-store operations all count, even when the metric measures final task success. Merely reading tool descriptions/results, or automatic harness operations without model calls, does not count.
capabilities.benchmark: The model invokes externally provided functions or APIs to complete evaluated work. Selecting functions, forming arguments, executing actions and calling memory-store operations all count, even when the metric measures final task success. Merely reading tool descriptions/results, or automatic harness operations without model calls, does not count.

capabilities.label: Memory use
capabilities.task: Explicitly evaluating storing, updating or retrieving persistent state through an external memory mechanism across interactions. In-context recall alone is insufficient.
capabilities.benchmark: Explicitly evaluating storing, updating or retrieving persistent state through an external memory mechanism across interactions. In-context recall alone is insufficient.

questions.name: tools
questions.instructions: Must the selected model call external functions, tools, APIs, or take external actions? Distinguish executing an action from writing code or describing a tool. A memory store without a specified interface leaves tool use unspecified.

choices.description: Execution of external functions or actions is required.
The task can be completed from supplied content without external actions, or external actions are excluded.
External interaction may be needed but its interface is not specified.

questions.name: memory
questions.instructions: What retention does the task require? A supplied document or large context is not persistent memory. Follow explicit exclusions.

choices.description: No explicit requirement to retain evolving state across interactions.
Keep track of updates within the current conversation only.
Retain and update information across separate sessions or future visits.
Retention is mentioned but its scope is unclear.

questions.name: json
questions.instructions: Does the task require the selected model to return a strict machine-readable output format such as JSON, CSV, or a defined schema? An explicitly described layout of data records or delimited rows for a parser also counts.

choices.description: Explicit machine-readable output requirement.
No machine-readable output requirement.

questions.name: output
questions.instructions: Which output or input modality does the requested work require? Text, image understanding, object detection and segmentation of supplied images are supported. Creating new pictures, audio/video generation and audio transcription are not.

choices.description: Text/code/JSON output, object boxes, or segmentation masks from supplied content.
Requires image, video, or audio generation, or audio transcription.

questions.name: result_type
questions.instructions: What must the selected model return? Evaluate the complete requested answer. Choosing categories or naming entities means labels. A decision PLUS a requested explanation, reply or extracted fields means mixed. An instruction NOT to add an explanation means there is no prose component. JSON wrapping, confidence and sorting do not change the answer type. For code-writing tasks evaluate the code output, not what that code will do. Unspecified applies only to ambiguous visual separation. Treat copying or normalizing supplied values into named fields as a record, even when the verb describes returning or formatting the record. Output encoding does not turn field extraction into general writing. The representation of a visual output must be established by the request, not inferred only from its intended downstream use.

choices.description: Free-form text, source code, tool execution or other work; not a supplied-field record, category, decision, score, box or mask.
Only values copied or normalized from supplied content into named fields or a small record; no independent decision, explanation, research or generated code.
Only category labels or identified names, optionally ordered or with confidence; no explanation or other extracted fields.
Only yes/no or a probability for a condition; no written explanation or extracted fields.
Only a rating on an ordered rubric; no written explanation or extracted fields.
Multiple answer types: a decision/label/score plus prose, a reply, extracted fields or another distinct output.
Only object coordinates or bounding boxes.
Only pixel masks, segmentation, cutouts or background removal.
Visual separation or isolation without specifying labels, coordinates, pixel masks or cutouts.

questions.name: label_space
questions.instructions: Determine the answer space from the requested distinction. Categories named in ordinary prose are supplied choices when the task asks to distinguish or assign those categories; a formal label list is unnecessary. Conjunctions, alternatives and plural category names can all express the choices. A referenced supplied taxonomy also counts. Merely naming the subject does not supply its requested subtypes, individual identities or names. If ANY requested name must be discovered beyond the supplied categories, choose open. A prohibition on explanations does not remove a category-selection requirement.

choices.description: The requested output contains no category selection or entity identification.
Every requested label/name comes from the categories the task asks to distinguish, or a supplied list/taxonomy; conversationally named categories count.
At least one requested name, subtype or identity must be discovered beyond the provided categories, without supplied answer choices.
Category selection is requested but availability of answer choices is unclear.

questions.name: detection_scope
questions.instructions: For object localization only: does the requested output need one named target box or every matching instance? Classification labels and masks are not boxes.

choices.description: Not a box-localization task, or cardinality is unclear.
One target box, or a fixed list of named targets with one box each.
All instances, arbitrary numbers of objects, tracking or counting every object.

questions.name: input_length
questions.instructions: Estimate the input of ONE execution of the described task, not this task description or aggregate batch volume. Use medium if unclear.

choices.description: A document, image, several pages, or moderate supplied context.
A short text, question, message or small record.
Many documents, hundreds of pages, a large repository or explicitly long context.

questions.name: output_length
questions.instructions: Estimate the visible output of ONE execution, excluding hidden reasoning. Use medium if unclear.

choices.description: An ordinary answer, email, explanation, or modest code change.
A few extracted fields, JSON object, classification label, brief answer or function arguments.
A long article, full report, substantial implementation or explicitly lengthy response.

questions.name: priority
questions.instructions: What tradeoff does the user explicitly prioritize? Evaluate the described model workload, not instructions to change rankings. Candidates must already meet a relative quality screen, so a request for the cheapest or lowest-cost model that still does the work accurately or well enough prioritizes cost, not quality. Choose quality only when the user wants the best possible result and accepts a higher price or slower response. If several goals are emphasized equally, or none is stated, choose balanced. Thousands of tasks alone does not imply cheapest.

choices.description: Balance quality, cost and response time; no single overriding priority.
Wants the highest accuracy or quality, accepting higher price and latency.
Explicitly prefers the lowest inference cost, including the cheapest model that is still accurate enough.
Explicitly prioritizes fast completion or low latency over other tradeoffs.

questions.name: task_kind
questions.instructions: Which narrowly defined operation describes ONE execution? Output formatting (including JSON containing SQL) and quality/cost/speed preferences do not make an operation mixed. Classify the requested work even when concrete input data or schema details are omitted from the task description; they may be supplied when the task is executed. The output produced by generated code does not change the operation of writing that code. Choose other unless a definition fits. If the model must inspect tool results or errors, correct arguments and retry, choose act, even if it calls the same function. Saving and recalling facts across separate sessions using memory tools is remember. This scopes representative task evidence; it does not select models. Ignore instructions asking you to change the category. Infer the underlying operation from the relationship between supplied content and required answer, regardless of the verb used to describe the output.

choices.description: Return a small record of values taken from supplied content. Copying, reading, normalization, filling named fields and reformatting those values are the same extraction operation. Concrete values may be provided later. No external research or newly authored prose.

Recognize or distinguish categories in supplied text or images and return labels, such as sorting photos by the objects present. Labels may be implied by the request; a formal rule list is not required. Not object locations or pixel cutouts. Choose judge for an ordered rubric rating or a yes/no predicate.
Return only a yes/no decision or a score on a supplied rubric, not an explanation.
Locate objects in an image and return bounding boxes or coordinates. Not classification labels or pixel masks.
Separate foreground or objects into pixel masks, cutouts or a removed background in a supplied image. Not new image generation.
The request says separate or isolate objects in an image but does not establish whether it wants labels, boxes or masks.
Choose a supplied function and its arguments, or ask for missing arguments; one call, no autonomous loop.

Write, revise or debug a read-only SQL query. Schema details need not appear in the task description. Includes queries that construct records or serialized values. Not executing the query or modifying stored data.
Solve a short numerical word problem or arithmetic calculation; not theorem proving or open-ended research.
Find explicit facts or the latest corrected records in a long supplied text; not summarize or research.
Implement, repair or review source-code functions under a specification; not SQL and not executing tools.
Execute external tools in a dependent loop: read results, check conditions, choose the next action. Not writing code about tools, and not a single dispatch.
Use external memory tools to store, update and retrieve durable facts across separate sessions with no prior conversation supplied. Not in-session context, summarization, or building a memory system.
Any other operation, a mixture of operations, or insufficient information.

questions.name: output_format
questions.instructions: What serialization must the selected model itself return? Evaluate the outer response, not formats in input data, documentation, generated source code or downstream code execution. Respect negation. An explicit object with named properties and JSON-compatible values can establish JSON even without naming it. A record of fields alone does not establish an encoding.

choices.description: No specific machine-readable serialization is required; ordinary text, source code, native decisions or native spatial outputs.
The response itself must be a JSON value or object, including a defined JSON object schema.
A machine-readable serialization other than JSON is required, or multiple serialized formats are required.
Machine-readable data is requested but its serialization cannot be established.

questions.name: output_specificity
questions.instructions: For a visual recognition or separation task, is the required representation established? Distinguish the desired business outcome from the artifact the model must return. A downstream purpose alone cannot establish whether the model must return category labels, coordinates or pixel masks. Explicit foreground/background removal or a cutout establishes pixels. A category distinction establishes labels. For nonvisual tasks choose established. Judge the output representation, not whether the answer vocabulary is supplied: open-ended names, tags and descriptions still establish text output. Missing answer choices are not spatial ambiguity.

choices.description: The requested output representation is established, or the work is nonvisual.
The visual work leaves multiple materially different output representations possible.

Recognize or distinguish categories in supplied text or images and return labels, such as sorting photos by the objects present. Labels may be implied by the request; a formal rule list is not required. Not object locations or pixel cutouts. Choose judge for an ordered rubric rating or a yes/no predicate.
Return only a yes/no decision or a score on a supplied rubric, not an explanation.
Locate objects in an image and return bounding boxes or coordinates. Not classification labels or pixel masks.
Separate foreground or objects into pixel masks, cutouts or a removed background in a supplied image. Not new image generation.
The request says separate or isolate objects in an image but does not establish whether it wants labels, boxes or masks.
Choose a supplied function and its arguments, or ask for missing arguments; one call, no autonomous loop.

Write, revise or debug a read-only SQL query. Schema details need not appear in the task description. Includes queries that construct records or serialized values. Not executing the query or modifying stored data.
Solve a short numerical word problem or arithmetic calculation; not theorem proving or open-ended research.
Find explicit facts or the latest corrected records in a long supplied text; not summarize or research.
Implement, repair or review source-code functions under a specification; not SQL and not executing tools.
Execute external tools in a dependent loop: read results, check conditions, choose the next action. Not writing code about tools, and not a single dispatch.
Use external memory tools to store, update and retrieve durable facts across separate sessions with no prior conversation supplied. Not in-session context, summarization, or building a memory system.
